summary: David Seyfort Ruegg (1931–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and Sorbonne University under Jean Filliozat, Louis Renou, Marcelle Lalou, and Rolf A. Stein. He held chairs and professorships at Leiden, Washington, Hamburg, and SOAS.

David Sneath works in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge, held a British Academy Postdoctoral Research Fellowship at the University of Oxford, and served as a Director at Cambridge from 2000 to 2009.
David Steindl-Rast (born 1926) is a religious studies scholar. Between approximately 1946 and 1952, he studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

David Tracy (1939–2025) was a scholar in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. After lecturing at the Catholic University of America, he was a longtime professor of Catholic studies at the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

David W. Chappell (1940–2004) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned degrees from Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale. He taught as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from ~1972 to 2002 and taught comparative studies at Soka University of America from ~2002 to 2004.

David W. Tien is a scholar in sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, earning a PhD at Michigan under James Robson and also studying under Robert H. Sharf.
David Webster works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) was a Tibetology and history scholar. He studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at San Francisco State University, the University of San Francisco, CIIS, and served as professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2006).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetologist who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Ex-Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at the University of the Punjab and Oriental College, he trained under John Marshall. He served as curator at Lucknow Museum, worked in Jammu and Kashmir, held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, and directed archaeology in Jaipur State.

Dayong (1893–1929) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. He studied at Wuchang Buddhist Institute and under Taixu, Bai Puren, and Dpal ldan bstan 'dzin snyan grags. He taught at Wuchang Buddhist Institute (1923) and founded the Tibetan Studies College.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as its director in 1988, and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) was an Indologist and philosopher. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1956–1978) and served as a guest professor at the University of Calcutta.
Deborah Carlson is a scholar in history and archaeology who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (both attested 2015).

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian of Asia working in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at Harvard under Oleg Grabar and completed her Habilitation at the University of Vienna, where she held the Chair of Asian Art History from 1994 to 2015.
Declan Quigley works in Indology and religious studies. He has held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.
Dedong Wei (born 1968) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China and served there as an associate professor of religious studies around 2002.
Demchok Dorje studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.
